Live free in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "website builder for hair salons", "category": "Industries", "bodyHtml": "

Most hair salon websites are either a dated template with a stock photo of someone else's salon, or a single Instagram link pretending to be a homepage. Neither tells a new client what they actually want to know: what you charge, who's cutting their hair, and whether the work looks good. Kodely builds that site for you in one chat conversation, as a real coded app, not a mockup.

What Hair Salon Websites Actually Need

Before someone books a chair, they're comparing you to three other salons in a browser tab. In the first ten seconds they're scanning for the same handful of things: your price list, proof that your stylists are good, recent photos of real haircuts and color work, your hours and location, and a simple way to reach out. A slow template site or a Facebook page buried under old posts loses that comparison every time.

The Must-Have Sections

  • Services and pricing — a clear, scannable list so people aren't guessing before they call.
  • Stylist bios — names, specialties, and a short line of personality build trust fast.
  • Gallery of work — before/after cuts and color, styled the way your actual site will look.
  • Hours and location — the basics, front and center, no digging required.
  • Booking inquiry form — a simple way for a visitor to request an appointment.

A Real Prompt You Can Use

Kodely works from plain-English descriptions, so specificity is what separates a generic result from a site that actually looks like your salon. Here's a prompt that produces a strong first draft:

Build a website for Willow & Co, a boutique hair salon in a warm, editorial style with cream, sage, and charcoal colors. Include a homepage with a hero section and a call to action to book, a services and pricing page for cuts, color, balayage, and styling, a stylist bios page with photos and specialties, a gallery page for before-and-after work, and a contact page with hours, location, and a booking inquiry form.

That single prompt gives Kodely enough structure to generate a multi-page site with a consistent layout, rather than one long scrolling homepage.

What Kodely Generates

Kodely doesn't output a static HTML template. It writes a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app, built from a foundation codebase of hand-built UI components. From the prompt above, you'd get actual component files for the hero section, a services table, a stylist bio grid, an image gallery layout, and a contact section with a booking inquiry form UI. You watch the real compiled app render in a live preview as it's generated.

One clarification worth being direct about: the booking inquiry form captures a request through the UI — it isn't a connected scheduling and payment system with calendar sync. It's the front door for a client to reach out; you handle confirming the appointment. If you want to see how that pattern gets used in practice, the guide to building a booking appointment website with AI walks through it in more detail.

Customizing Your Salon Site

Once the first draft is generated, refine it the same way you created it: describe the change in chat. Swap the color palette, rewrite a stylist bio, reorder the services list, or add a page for gift cards — Kodely edits the real component files behind the scenes. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change doesn't land right, rolling back is free and instant. You can also open the code view at any point to see and copy the actual generated source files.

Publishing It Live

When the site looks right, publishing is one click. Kodely puts it live at a free yoursalon.kodely.site address — no separate hosting account, no server setup, no extra cost. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked API keys or secrets before it goes live, so you're not shipping something you'll regret. Custom domains and code export aren't available yet, but the site is fully live and shareable the moment you publish.

FAQ

Does Kodely build a working booking and payment system?

Not yet. Kodely generates the services, pricing, stylist bios, gallery, and a booking inquiry form as real UI — a client can request an appointment through the form, but there's no connected calendar, scheduling engine, or payment processing behind it.

What does it cost to build and publish a salon site?

Signing up gives you 750 free credits, no credit card required, which is enough to generate and publish a first version. If you need more, top-ups start at $9 for 500 credits, and credits never expire. A build that fails to compile is never charged.

Can I use my own domain instead of kodely.site?

Not currently. Every published site gets a free subdomain at yourname.kodely.site.

Can I edit the code myself?

You can view and copy the generated source files from the in-app code view. Downloading a full project as a zip isn't supported yet — editing happens through chat.

What if I want to change something after publishing?

Describe the change in chat and Kodely updates the real components, then you republish. Every version is checkpointed, so you can roll back for free if a change doesn't work out.

See pricing for the full credit breakdown, or browse the blog for more build guides. Ready to see your salon's site take shape? Build your salon site free.
